memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses and Aaron and his sons were to camp to the east of the tabernacle, toward the sunrise, in front of the tent of meeting. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Anyone else who approached the sanctuary was to be put to death. - Num 3:38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses, Aaron, and the priests camped on the east side, in front of the entrance, closest to the sanctuary. They held the place of nearest access and greatest responsibility. They stood, as it were, on the front line of God's presence, guarding the way in on behalf of the whole nation.

Once more we meet that solemn warning: anyone unauthorised who approached was to be put to death. The way into God's presence was carefully protected. This is not something to explain away or soften — it shows how truly holy God is, and how impossible it is for sinful people to stroll casually into His presence.

Yet notice where the priests camped: toward the sunrise, facing the dawn. Even in this careful guarding of holiness, there is a hint of hope, of light breaking in.

That hope is fulfilled in Jesus. He is our great High Priest who not only guards the way to God but opens it. Through His death, the barrier came down, and He now brings us near (Heb 7:25). The One who camped closest to the presence points to the One who has become our way into the presence forever.

So we come to God today not by our own worthiness, but through Christ — welcomed, brought near, and safe.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you grasp how holy God is, and how amazing your access is?
- How does Jesus, your High Priest, bring you near to God?
- What does it mean to face the "sunrise" of hope in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, thank You that through Jesus, my great High Priest, I can come near to You. I do not take this access lightly; I receive it with wonder. Amen.
